rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asr can denote absolute or present time, a generation or ruler's era, night, morning, evening, afternoon, the afternoon prayer, or a religious period.
rows.anchor: Asr (asır) kelimesi isim olarak “mutlak zaman, içinde bulunulan zaman, karn (80 veya 100 yıllık zaman dilimi)

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Commentators have read asr as afternoon, the afternoon prayer, absolute time, Muhammad's era, or the end times.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler burada zikredilen asr kelimesini ikindi vakti, ikindi namazı, mutlak zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary prefers absolute time as the meaning best suited to the surah's content and message.
rows.anchor: Bize göre bunlar içinde sûrenin içeriğine ve mesajına en uygun düşeni “mutlak zaman” anlamıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by time calls attention to its place and importance in human life and as the arena where God's acts manifest His existence and boundless power.
rows.anchor: Zamana yemin edilerek onun insan hayatındaki yerine ve önemine dikkat çekilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For humans, time is the condition of life and a field of opportunity in which they can carry out every kind of action.
rows.anchor: insan bakımından da hayatını içinde geçirdiği ve her türlü eylemlerini gerçekleştirebildiği bir imkân ve fırsatlar alanıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by this precious reality to stress time's value and warn that a person who fails to use it well ends in loss.
rows.anchor: zamanın önemine dikkat çekmiş; onu iyi değerlendirmeyen insanın sonunun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, loss means the punishment of the hereafter, the greatest loss for someone who has wasted life and time, as Ibn Ashur is cited.
rows.anchor: Burada “ziyan”la âhiret azabı kastedilmiştir. Çünkü zamanı ve ömrü boşa geçirmiş insan için en büyük ziyan odur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere faith is the first trait that saves people from loss; the commentary refers readers to other passages on faith.
rows.anchor: Samimi bir şekilde iman etmek (iman hakkında bk. Kur’an Yolu, Bakara 2/256; Nisâ 4/136-137)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beneficial deeds for this world and the hereafter mean doing what religion, reason, and conscience command and avoiding what they forbid.
rows.anchor: Dünya ve âhiret için yararlı işler yapmak, yani din, akıl ve vicdanın emrettiklerini yerine getirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counseling one another to uphold truth is a further quality that saves from loss.
rows.anchor: Hakkı tavsiye etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counseling one another to be patient is a further quality that saves from loss.
rows.anchor: Sabrı tavsiye etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good works already include urging truth and patience, but these are named separately because they show virtue and responsibility toward others and produce social benefit.
rows.anchor: hem bireyin erdemini ve hemcinslerine karşı sorumluluk bilincini yansıttığı hem de bireyi aşarak toplumsal yararlar doğurduğu için önemi dolayısıyla ayrıca zikredilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to counsel truth and patience also implies that a person must first follow these duties; this is too obvious to require explicit statement.
rows.anchor: bu görevlere kişinin öncelikle kendisinin uyması gerektiği anlamının da bulunduğu kuşkusuzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counseling truth and patience illuminates education's importance, nature, and purpose: education transmits truth in belief, knowledge, and ethics and builds resilience against hardship, error, and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: Doğru bir eğitim faaliyetinin amacı ise insanlara inançta, bilgide ve ahlâkta hakkı yani gerçeği ve doğruyu aktarmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth and patience encompass the moral duties of social life; truth opposes falsehood and is linked to justice and a social order that protects everyone's rights.
rows.anchor: hak, adaletle de yakından ilişkilidir. Bu açıdan âyette insanların âdil olmaları ve adalet düzeninin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through faith and good works a servant fulfills God's rights, and through mutual counsel in truth and patience fulfills the rights of other people.
rows.anchor: iman ve sâlih amel sayesinde Allah’ın hakkını, hakkı ve sabrı tavsiye ile de kulların hakkını ödemiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite its brevity, Surah al-Asr contains a rich summary of the Qur'an's religious and moral duties and counsels.
rows.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’deki bütün dinî ve ahlâkî yükümlülüklerin, öğütlerin özü sayılmaya değer

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i is quoted as saying that this short surah alone would suffice humanity if nothing else had been revealed, since it embraces all Qur'anic sciences.
rows.anchor: Şayet Kur’an’da başka bir şey nâzil olmasaydı, şu pek kısa sûre bile insanlara yeterdi. Bu sûre Kur’an’ın bütün ilimlerini kucaklıyor

rows.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
rows.claim: Akif's poem presents true faith, righteous conduct, truth, and steadfastness as the sequence that saves humanity from loss.
rows.anchor: Başta îmân-ı hakîkî geliyor sonra salâh Sonra hak sonra sebât: İşte kuzum insanlık Dördü birleşti mi yoktur sana hüsrân artık

rows.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
rows.claim: Akif's poem says the Companions would recite Surah al-Asr when they were about to part.
rows.anchor: Hani ashâb-ı kirâm ayrılalım derlerken Mutlaka sûre-i ve’l-Asr’ı okurmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After condemning failure in one's duties toward people, the surah criticizes those who fail to fulfill genuine duties of worship toward God.
rows.anchor: Yukarıda insanlara karşı insanlık görevini yerine getirmeyenler kınanmıştı; burada ise Allah’a karşı gerçek anlamda kulluk görevlerini yerine getirmeyenler eleştirilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three faults are given among people who pray: distance from prayer's essence, ostentation in worship, and obstructing good.
rows.anchor: Namazlarının özünden uzak olmaları, b) İbadetlerinde halka gösteriş yapmaları, c) Hayra engel olmaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sahun literally means forgetful; some interpret it here as those who fail to pray on time.
rows.anchor: sâhûn kelimesinin sözlük anlamı “unutanlar” olup bu bağlamda, “namazlarını vaktinde kılmayanlar” şeklinde yorumlayanlar bulunmuşsa da

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari takes sahun to mean people who disregard prayer and prefer other activities, a reading that also includes delaying prayer or abandoning it.
rows.anchor: Taberî, bizim de meâlde esas aldığımız yorumunda sâhûn kelimesini, “namazı ciddiye almayanlar, başka şeylerle meşgul olmayı namaz kılmaya tercih edenler” şeklinde anlamanın daha isabetli olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riya is presenting a religious or moral virtue one lacks and pursuing material or spiritual gain through apparent goodness.
rows.anchor: bir kimsenin, kendisinde bulunmayan dinî ve ahlâkî bir meziyeti, bir erdemi varmış gibi göstermesi

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari reports that ma'un has been explained as alms, other financial duties, benefits people withhold from each other, a right, a loan, or property.
rows.anchor: zekât, diğer malî yükümlülükler, insanların kendi aralarında birbirine yararlandırmadıkları nimetler, hak, ödünç, mal

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari understands ma'un broadly as kindness, good, and sharing benefits; the authors likewise render it with the broad word “good.”
rows.anchor: insanlara iyilik, hayır, nimetlerin paylaşılması gibi anlamları kuşatan genel bir ifade olduğunu belirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outward forms of worship remain essential, but equal care is due to its inner substance: faith, intention, sincerity, reverence, and piety.
rows.anchor: şekil şartları da vazgeçilmez olmakla birlikte, en az şekil kadar özen gösterilmesi gereken husus

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intention and sincerity in worship reflect the principle of divine unity, as illustrated by the cited verses.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’a göre ibadetlerde niyet ve ihlâs, tevhid ilkesinin ibadetteki yansımasıdır

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: The Prophet describes worship as serving God as though one sees Him.
rows.anchor: Bunu Hz. Peygamber, “Allah’ı görüyormuşçasına ibadet etmek” şeklinde belirtmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah stresses that sincere worship of God and mutual aid and solidarity cannot be separated in religious devotion.
rows.anchor: Allah’a gönülden ibadet etmekle yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın dindarlıkta birbirinden ayrılmazlığının vurgulanmış olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A truly believing person fulfills duties toward God and creation sincerely, does good, and enables rather than blocks its spread through social cooperation.
rows.anchor: yardımlaşma ve dayanışmanın önünü tıkayan değil, aksine gelişip yaygınlaşmasına, bireyselliği aşarak toplumsal ve kurumsal bir yapı kazanmasına katkıda bulunan insandır

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh reports that before this ruling people could eat, drink, and have intercourse until they slept; Qays ibn Sirma slept after the evening prayer without food and woke exhausted, while Umar had intercourse after sleeping and told the Prophet; the verse then came.
rows.anchor: قال كانوا يأكلون ويشربون ويأتون النساء ما لم يناموا فإذا ناموا امتنعوا ثم ان رجلا من الأنصار يقال له قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report through Ibn Abi Layla from Muadh is well known, though Ibn Abi Layla did not hear directly from Muadh; it has corroborating reports.
rows.anchor: هذا الحديث مشهور عن ابن أبي ليلى لكنه لم يسمع من معاذ وله شواهد

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara reports that anyone who slept before breaking the fast could not eat that night or the next day; Qays's wife sought food while he worked, he slept, and he fainted the following day before the verse permitted night intimacy and food until dawn.
rows.anchor: كان أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا كان الرجل صائما فحضر الإفطار فنام قبل أن يفطر لم يأكل ليلته ولا يومه حتى يمسي

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara also reports that when Ramadan fasting was first prescribed, men abstained from women for the entire month and some betrayed themselves, prompting the clause about God forgiving them.
rows.anchor: لما نزل صوم شهر رمضان كانوا لا يقربون النساء رمضان كله فكان رجال يخونون أنفسهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b reports that after sleeping, Ramadan fasting forbade food, drink, and sex until the next sunset; Umar and Ka'b each had intercourse after sleep, and Umar informed the Prophet, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: كان الناس في رمضان إذا صام الرجل فأمسى فنام حرم عليه الطعام والشراب والنساء حتى يفطر من الغد

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl reports that the initial wording lacked “at dawn”; some tied white and black threads to their legs and kept eating until they could distinguish them, then the clarification showed that night and day were meant.
rows.anchor: أنزلت ﴿ وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض من الخيط الأسود ﴾ ولم ينزل من الفجر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a person in retreat could leave the mosque and have intercourse if he wished, prompting the prohibition on intimacy during retreat in mosques.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل اذا اعتكف فخرج من المسجد جامع إن شاء فنزلت ﴿ ولا تباشروهن وأنتم عاكفون في المساجد ﴾

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that Imru al-Qays ibn Abis and Abdan ibn Ashwa al-Hadrami disputed over land, and the former wanted to swear an oath when the prohibition on consuming property unjustly was revealed.
rows.anchor: إن امرأ القيس بن عابس وعبدان بن أشوع الحضرمي اختصما في أرض وأراد امرأ القيس أن يحلف ففيه نزلت

rows.speaker: رافع
rows.claim: Rafi says the verse about rejoicing in one's deeds concerned hypocrites who stayed behind from the Prophet, made excuses, and wished they had gone with the believers; when Marwan challenged him, Zayd ibn Thabit affirmed his account.
rows.anchor: قال رافع أنزلت في أناس من المنافقين كانوا إذا خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتذروا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar says the report from Rafi can be reconciled with Ibn Abbas's account by allowing the verse to have concerned both groups.
rows.anchor: يجمع بين هذا وبين قول ابن عباس بأنه يمكن أن تكون نزلت في الفريقين معا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says it concerned Jews who claimed to be the earlier people of scripture, prayer, and obedience while refusing to acknowledge Muhammad; several Successors reported similar accounts.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء أنها نزلت في قول اليهود نحن أهل الكتاب الأول والصلاة والطاعة ومع ذلك لا يقرون بمحمد

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Tabari preferred the interpretation that the verse concerned the Jews, while allowing that it could have been revealed about all these groups.
rows.anchor: ورجحه ابن جرير ولا مانع أن تكون نزلت في كل ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews about Moses's signs and Christians about Jesus's miracles, then asked Muhammad to turn Safa into gold; the verse directed them to reflect on signs in creation.
rows.anchor: أتت قريش اليهود فقالوا بم جاءكم موسى من الآيات قالوا عصاه ويد بيضاء للناظرين وأتوا النصارى

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab reports that Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, and Khabbab when Arab delegations arrived; the verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed.
rows.anchor: جاء الأقرع ابن حابس وعيينة بن حصن فوجدا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صهيب وبلال وعمار وخباب قاعدا في ناس من الضعفاء

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: The same report says the Prophet would leave the poor believers when he stood, after which the instruction to keep himself with those who call upon their Lord was revealed.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس معنا فاذا أراد أن يقوم قام وتركنا فنزل ﴿ واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report unusual because the verse is Meccan while Aqra and Uyayna converted much later, after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير هذا حديث غريب فإن الآية مكية والأقرع وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر

rows.speaker: ماهان
rows.claim: Mahan reports that people with grave sins came to the Prophet, who gave no answer, and the verse instructing him to greet believers who come with God's signs was revealed.
rows.anchor: جاء ناس إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا إنا أصبنا ذنوبا عظاما فما رد عليهم شيئا فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: سيار أبو الحكم
rows.claim: Sayyar reports that after receiving a large grain donation, the Prophet generously distributed it; when people arrived after it was gone, the verse against stinginess and excessive spending was revealed.
rows.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بر وكان معطيا كريما فقسمه بين الناس فأتاه قوم فوجدوه قد فرغ منه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that a boy asked the Prophet for his shirt on his mother's behalf; he gave it away and sat at home bare, prompting the verse against either hoarding or spending everything.
rows.anchor: جاء غلام إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إن أمي تسألك كذا وكذا قال ما عندنا شيء اليوم

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama reports that the Prophet told Aisha to spend everything on the back of her hand; she replied that nothing would remain, and the verse followed. The report suggests it was Medinan.
rows.anchor: ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لعائشة أنفق ما على ظهر كفي قالت إذن لا يبقى شيء فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: The occasion for “keep yourself with those who call upon their Lord” was already given in the account from Khabbab in Surah al-An'am.
rows.anchor: تقدم سبب النزول في سورة الأنعام في حديث خباب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the instruction not to obey one whose heart is heedless concerned Umayya ibn Khalaf, who wanted the Prophet to expel the poor and favor Makkan leaders.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أمية بن خلف الجمحي وذلك أنه دعا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى أمر كرهه الله من طرد الفقراء عنه وتقريب صناديد أهل مكة

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the Prophet turned his attention to Umayya ibn Khalaf, who was inattentive to what he was being told, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تصدى لأمية بن خلف وهو ساه غافل عما يقال له فنزلت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Uyayna ibn Hisn entered while Salman was with the Prophet and demanded that Salman be removed when Uyayna's party arrived; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: دخل عيينة بن حصن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده سلمان فقال عيينة إذا نحن أتيناك فأخرج هذا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Quraysh used to replace a stone idol with a more attractive one and worship the new object, prompting the verse about taking one's desire as a god.
rows.anchor: كانت قريش تعبد الحجر حينا من الدهر فإذا وجدوا ما هو أحسن منه طرحوا الأول وعبدوا الآخر فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that people of the pre-Islamic era said only night and day destroy them, and the verse about attributing death to time was revealed.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يقولون إنما يهلكنا الليل والنهار فأنزل الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews questioned Muhammad about creation; after he described creation over six days, they said he had answered correctly only if he finished by saying God rested. The Prophet became angry and the verses denying weariness and commanding patience were revealed.
rows.anchor: قالت اليهود ثم ماذا يا محمد قال ثم استوى على العرش قالوا قد أصبت لو أتممت قالوا ثم استراح فغضب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that people asked the Prophet to warn them, and the instruction to remind through the Qur'an those who fear God's warning was revealed.
rows.anchor: قالوا يا رسول الله لو خوفتنا فنزلت ﴿ فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد ﴾

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A mursal report from Umar gives the same occasion for the command to remind people through the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ثم أخرج عن عمر مرسلا مثله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that a palm owner repeatedly took fruit from poor children beneath a tree whose branches crossed their courtyard; the Prophet offered him a tree in Paradise, another man bought the palm for forty trees and transferred it to the Prophet, who gave it to the poor family. The surah was then revealed; Ibn Kathir calls the report very unusual.
rows.anchor: فكان الرجل إذا جاء الدار فصعد إلى النخلة ليأخذ منها الثمرة فربما تقع ثمرة فيأخذها صبيان الفقير

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Abu Bakr's father that he urged Abu Bakr to free strong enslaved men who could defend him rather than weak ones; Abu Bakr said he sought God's reward, and the verses beginning “the one who gives and is mindful” were revealed about him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو قحافة لأبي بكر أراك تعتق رقابا ضعافا فلو أنك أعتقت رجالا جلدا يمنعونك ويقومون دونك

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr freed seven people who were being tortured for God, and the verse about the most Godfearing being kept away from the Fire was revealed about this.
rows.anchor: أن أبا بكر الصديق اعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في اللهوفيه نزلت ﴿ وسيجنبها الأتقى ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reports that the verse stating no one had a favor to repay, through the end, was revealed about Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: قال نزلت هذه الآية ﴿ وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى ﴾ إلى آخرها في أبي بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: جندب
rows.claim: Jundub reports that when the Prophet was ill and did not rise for one or two nights, a woman said his Satan had abandoned him, and the opening verses of al-Duha were revealed.
rows.anchor: اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين فأتته امرأة فقالت يا محمد ما أرى شيطانك إلا قد تركك

rows.speaker: جندب
rows.claim: In another report, Gabriel was delayed and the polytheists said Muhammad had been abandoned, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال المشركون قد ودع محمد فنزلت

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports that after Gabriel did not descend for days, Umm Jamil, Abu Lahab's wife, said the Prophet had been abandoned and rejected, and the verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: مكث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما لا ينزل عليه جبريل فقالت أم جميل امرأة أبي لهب

rows.speaker: خولة
rows.claim: Khawla's report says a dead puppy under the bed delayed revelation for four days; after it was removed Gabriel came, and verses through “until you are satisfied” were revealed.
rows.anchor: أن جروا دخل بيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل تحت السرير فمات فمكث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعة أيام لا ينزل عليه الوحي

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar says the puppy story as a cause of revelation is unusual and anomalous, rejected because it conflicts with sound reports, although the delay due to a puppy is well known.
rows.anchor: ولكن كونها سبب نزول الآية غريب بل شاذ مردود بما في الصحيح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
rows.claim: Abdullah ibn Shaddad reports that Khadija told the Prophet she thought his Lord had rejected him, and then the surah was revealed; this report is mursal.
rows.anchor: أن خديجة قالت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أرى ربك إلا قد قلاك فنزلت

rows.speaker: عروة
rows.claim: Urwa's mursal report says delayed revelation distressed the Prophet and Khadija compassionately told him she thought his Lord had rejected him; Ibn Hajar says Umm Jamil said it spitefully while Khadija said it out of concern.
rows.anchor: لكن أم جميل قالته شماتة وخديجة قالته توجعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses were said to have been revealed when polytheists taunted Muslims for their poverty.
rows.anchor: نزلت لما عير المشركون المسلمين بالفقر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that when “with hardship comes ease” was revealed, the Prophet announced that ease had come and one hardship would never overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت هذه الآية ﴿ إن مع العسر يسرا ﴾ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبشروا أتاكم اليسر لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says “returned him to the lowest of the low” concerned people in the Prophet's time who reached extreme old age; when their minds failed, God excused them and preserved the reward of their earlier deeds.
rows.anchor: قال هم نفر ردوا إلى أرذل العمر على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فسئل عنهم حين سفهت عقولهم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl vowed to trample Muhammad's neck and rub his face in dust if he saw him prostrating, prompting the verse that humanity transgresses.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جهل هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم فقيل نعم فقال واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يفعل لأطأن على رقبته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl came upon the Prophet praying and forbade him, prompting the passage about the one who forbids a servant when he prays through the sinful, lying forelock.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاءه أبو جهل فنهاه فأنزل الله ﴿ أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet while he prayed and boasted of his powerful assembly, the verses threatening to summon the guards were revealed; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو جهل إنك لتعلم ما بها ناد أكثر مني فأنزل الله ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال الترمذي حسن صحيح

rows.speaker: ابن بريدة
rows.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Ansar tribes Banu Haritha and Banu al-Harith competed by boasting about their living members, then went to the graves and boasted of the dead; the surah was revealed.
rows.anchor: نزلت في قبيلتين من الأنصار في بني حارثة وبني الحرث تفاخروا وتكاثروا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Muslims doubted punishment in the grave until the passage from “competition distracts you” through “then you will know” was revealed regarding that punishment.
rows.anchor: كنا نشك في عذاب القبر حتى نزلت ﴿ ألهاكم التكاثر ﴾ إلى ﴿ ثم كلا سوف تعلمون ﴾ في عذاب القبر
